notes: Annotated typescript with manuscript page 5 and archive sheet number 13 (comment only). Two displayed formulas occur, with the intermediate i*(H-group), proof decompositions and final restriction map inline. Section 4 starts below the proof. There is no new title, date or total page count.

The live text assumes conditions a) and b) for the geometric-fibre morphism and introduces a cycle z in Z^n(Y) whose geometric-fibre cycle is algebraically, hence cohomologically, equivalent to zero. It asserts that u(z) lies in the i*-image modulo a torsion class after replacing S by a nonempty open. The source reservation is “restriction probablement inutile, mais cet énoncé nous suffira pour ce qu’on veut en faire”; probablement replaces the cancelled sans doute.

The top insertion literally reads i_bar-s:X_bar-s→X_bar-s. The main crop confirms both X letters. Given i:Y→X on scan013, a direct check of the definition of base change gives an induced Y_bar-s→X_bar-s; this supports S’s proposed mathematical correction but does not alter the diplomatic text. H already calls attention to the expected source in its commentary.

The proof invokes 2), a curve/correspondence over a finite K/k(s), a trace argument, spreading after a possible open restriction, and z=i*(z′)+z″. It claims the cohomological action associated with z″ is zero and invokes 1) for u(z″)=0. These are reported as source steps, not independently proved. R3 checked only the conditional degree calculation 1+2n−2=2n−1 for a codimension-n correspondence over a curve.

The first displayed group is missing one terminal parenthesis, and the inline i*(H-group) is also missing an outer close. Their actual ink is retained. The inline coefficient has a possible pen Q over typed Z; plain Z remains possible. This is consequential for reading the trace step, but expected coefficient mathematics has not been used to settle it.

The two ambient-product capitals have different visible correction structures and remain separately uncertain. The first favours a doubled-X approximation; the second has a Y-like fork and central stem overlapping X-like legs, so both possible old/live orders are recorded. The intervening curve name similarly retains C/Z structural alternatives.

The old upper lines and the wrapped quitte à prendre l’adhérence du cycle are substantially readable under cancellation. Doubt remains in pouvoir/pourvoir and at the terminal a’s cancellation boundary. The old d in construction and the old é in hyp-é-erplanes are recoverable. The terminal t of définit remains literal. Overlapping d/l, d/s and m/l components are recorded without imposing a certain correction sequence; the latter component in Im was missed by both witnesses and all three reader texts.

Section 4 introduces a projective smooth scheme of dimension m, adds sur k Alg. clos, takes a Lefschetz pencil, writes the blown-up map to P^1_k, and chooses an open base for its smooth restriction. Both the pen comma after clos and the surviving typed comma after m remain. The open-base glyph is closest to B, with S/U/doubled-S alternatives, and the same visible form recurs in the final map. The map label j/f and clipped S-like target remain uncertain.

The extended stroke above b in fibres meets the letter’s irregular retraced bowl. It is treated as a probable pen retouch with a source-layer doubt, not as a detached authorial drawing. H’s missing handwriting wrapper alone is not counted as an error. Global machine-ell, constant-sheaf and emphasis conventions are credited throughout; physical missing words, correction layers, punctuation, alphabets and baseline x signs are compared separately.
